newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota grain terminals prepare for high water.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota grain terminals prepare for high water.

text.p: Grain terminals are preparing for high water on rivers near Minneapolis by making plans for sandbagging operations and evacuating facilities, grain officials said.

The Continental Grain Co elevator at Savage, Minn., on the Minnesota River was operating Friday but may have to close next week if flood waters close an access road to the terminal, a Continental spokesman said.
High water is preventing the terminal from loading grain barges, but so far the facility has not been damaged by the rising river.

The St Paul District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers expects the Minnesota River level to reach 23 feet within 24 hours in western Minnesota, nine feet above flood stage. Rainfall has been forecast for most of Minnesota and western Wisconsin for this weekend, the Corps said late Friday.
"The rapid (snow) melt and forecast rainfall will result in much higher crests on the Minnesota, Mississippi, and St Croix Rivers," the Corps said.
At Savage, Minn., the Minnesota was forecast to rise 1.2 feet in the next 24 hours. However, the Corps said the river should crest below the record set in 1993.
A Minnneapolis grain merchandiser said some local terminals could be closed Monday due to high river levels if the forecast rainfall occurs.

"Some elevators will have water in them, but some of the others will not be able to load rail because the tracks will be under water or the river's getting too high so they can't load the barges," said a Minneapolis grain merchandiser.
